text:
Devon: FYI seeing NVLink/PCIe DMA spikes on shared-slice-usw2-7 during bursts from a couple tenants. 95p token latency up ~150-200ms. Window: 2026-03-20 03:18 UTC. :grimacing:
Priya: Which tenants? Any pattern on seq len or request size?
Devon: t-aurora and t-boreal. Lots of tiny requests (seq < 64), high kvcache miss churn and streaming churn. NVLink peer stats pegged (~90%+).
Marco: If it's cross-GPU NVLink traffic, moving to another rack won't help. We need to reduce inter-GPU KV traffic or give them fenced NVLink headroom.
Sanjay: Two short-term options: (1) soft-shape egress per-tenant (burst tokens + token bucket) or (2) carveout ephemeral dedicated slice (prewarmed) with NVLink reservation.
Tess: Soft-shape seems least disruptive. Can we do automated detection -> soft-shape for X seconds -> monitor?
Devon: I prototyped a rule locally: if nvlink_util > 0.8 && tenant_kv_miss_rate > 0.5 for 90s -> tag tenant and apply policer. Worked on dev cluster.
Devon: Sample policer command we used:
```
# apply egress policer
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/tenants/t-aurora/policer -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" -d '{"egress_tps": 200, "burst": 400, "duration_s": 30}'
```
Priya: Nice. Any client errors observed when shaping?
Devon: None in dev canary. We saw slightly higher tail on some requests but overall 95p dropped back to baseline.
Marco: Need to consider detection false positives. Could be warmup storms from model swaps. How do we distinguish warmup vs sustained noisy tenant?
Sanjay: Add ramp detection: require sustained for 2m or repeated triggers within 15m. Also tag with reason = "nvlink_kv_churn" so we can audit.
Tess: For automation, propose this flow: detect -> soft-shape -> if recovers, remove tag; if persists >10m, schedule ephemeral carveout + prewarm and notify finance/CS.
Priya: Cost check: ephemeral 8xA100 carveout (prewarmed) ~ $600/day estimate (binocular estimate using current reserved pricing). We'll need finance sign-off for longer trials.
Devon: I drafted a prometheus alert rule for detection:
```
groups:
- name: infra-noise
  rules:
  - alert: NVLinkNoisyTenant
    expr: avg_over_time(nvlink_link_util{pod=\"gpu\"}[2m]) > 0.8 and avg_over_time(tenant_kvcache_miss_rate[2m]) > 0.5
    for: 90s
    labels:
      severity: warning
    annotations:
      summary: "Potential noisy tenant causing NVLink pressure"
```
Marco: We should push that rule behind a feature flag and run in dry-run to gather signal for 48h before auto-action.
Sanjay: I'll open a PR to noise-detector to add labeling hooks and soft-shape executor.
Tess: I'll prepare a canary run plan (dev -> staging -> prod) and add rollback steps. Soft-shape rollback = remove policer; carveout rollback = teardown prewarm and migrate back.
infra-bot: Incident INC-20260320-17 created, alerted #eng-infra and paged oncall.
Priya: Also consider fallback routing: route affected requests to a quantized/low-kv model variant while we remediate. That reduces NVLink pressure without slicing.
Devon: Good point. We have lighter variants for most gen models. We'll need runtime routing rule: if tenant_tag=egress_heavy -> prefer variant with lower KV footprint.
Marco: Long term: add 'egress_profile' to tenant metadata (low/medium/high) to prefer dedicated capacity for high. Also surface to sales so customers can opt-in.
Sanjay: Action items:
- Sanjay: PR to noise-detector (labeling + soft-shape executor) (ETA: today)
- Tess: Canary plan and playbook (ETA: tomorrow)
- Priya: Cost model + ops-approval for ephemeral carveouts (ETA: EOD)
- Marco: Routing change spec (variant fallback) (ETA: 48h)
Devon: I'll run a 30m dry-run of prometheus rule in dev and collect metrics.
Tess: Remember to add audit log entries for any auto-tagging to keep CS/Legal happy.
Priya: I'll draft short CS note offering customers trial of dedicated slice if they'd like us to move them proactively.
Devon: Thanks. We'll reconvene in 2 hours for status. :thumbsup:
